1. Claim 15 (Currently amended): A method for selecting an edge server computer from a plurality of server computers in a computer network for sending data to a client computer, the method comprising the steps of:
providing a locator of a resource on a second server computer, the locator including information indicative of at least one server computer of a first set of one or more server computers, the resource having a unique signature as part of its identifier;
__wherein the information indicative of at least one server computer is dynamically determined based on real-time server load metrics and network latency measurements__;
selecting the first server computer based on the information added to the locator __and the real-time server load metrics and network latency measurements__; and
sending the data from the first server computer to the client computer.

2. Claim 16 (Currently amended): The method of claim 15, the second server computer being a Web application server comprising a Web page with a hyperlink referencing the data to be sent to the client computer, the hyperlink including a unique signature, the method further comprising the steps of selecting the hyperlink by the client computer, and subsequently generating an http request out of this hyperlink by a web browser, this http request containing the unique signature identifying a media request, __wherein the unique signature encodes server selection criteria including at least one of: server capacity, geographic location, or content type compatibility__.

3. Claim 17 (Original)

4. Claim 18 (Currently amended): The method of claim 17, the media request broker selecting the first server computer based on the information __and on dynamically updated server performance metrics received in real-time from the plurality of server computers__.
